A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Their complete main texts, equations, figures, tables, and appendices support comparison, including matching content across appendix renumbering and figure relocation.

before.justification: v1 reports original layerwise object-recognition analyses, spatial-representation interventions, and token-compression and RoPE-scaling experiments in Sections 3-5 and the appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical studies and their results in Sections 3-5 and Appendices E-H.

M1.justification: The layerwise logit-lens procedure, visual-decoder distillation loss, three RLE compression variants, and RoPE-scaling rule remain unchanged. The added connector justification does not introduce a new procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions retain the same training and evaluation coverage: GQA, TextVQA, VQAv2, ScienceQA, MMBench, POPE, What's Up, VSR, and COCO/GQA-spatial. No new dataset, task, or test scenario is evaluated.

E2.justification: Tables 1 and 2 retain the same uncompressed models, compression variants, and models with or without fine-tuning and RoPE scaling. ToME and additional compression methods are newly discussed, but no corresponding evaluated comparisons are reported.

E3.justification: The empirical splits, model configurations, metrics, training budgets, and testing procedures are unchanged. The 6,000 training steps and batch size of 16 highlighted in v2 Section 5.1 were already documented in v1 Appendix A.6.

E4.justification: The layerwise POPE analysis, object-erasure and direction-vector interventions, and temperature and loss-weight sensitivity studies are retained. The additional example displayed in Figure 3 already appeared in v1 Figure 13; it is not a new case study.

E5.justification: Both versions report averaging over ten 1,000-example GQA subsamples and performing 100 direction-vector samplings per relationship. The uncertainty displays remain unchanged, with no new seed, confidence-interval, or significance-testing information.

E6.justification: v2 Appendix G newly reports an analytical FLOPs ratio of 43.82% for LLaVA-1.5-7B at a compression ratio of 0.58. This is a calculated cost estimate, not a measured speedup. The existing empirical table values and plotted findings are unchanged.

T1.justification: v2 Appendix G adds computational-cost formulas for the original and compressed LLM, including visual-decoder overhead and explicit simplifying assumptions. The existing RoPE mathematics and spatial-representation derivations remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction retain the same four contributions concerning object recognition, spatial geometry, token compression, and RoPE scaling. The expanded conclusion explicitly names applications already claimed in v1.

C2.justification: Section 3.2 adds a residual-stream argument asserting the validity of applying the final-layer connector to earlier layers, while retaining the original connector limitation in Appendix A. Section 5.2 also explicitly characterizes RoPE scaling as a localized remedy.

D1.justification: v2 Section 5.1 newly discloses approximately five hours of visual-decoder training on an A40 GPU. The other highlighted training settings were already available in v1's appendix, and the code URL is unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds discussion and citations concerning ToME, additional compression approaches, superposition, sparse autoencoders, and causal tracing. Section 6 more explicitly positions the layerwise investigation relative to Joseph and Neo, without fundamentally changing the research framing.

P1.justification: v2 makes localized clarifications, expands related work and the conclusion, and adds acknowledgements and a dedicated LLM-use disclosure. Appendix A.1-A.7 becomes separate appendices A and C-H, while the main narrative structure remains intact.

P2.justification: Figure 3 expands from one example to two by reusing the skiing segmentation example already in v1 Figure 13. Figures and tables undergo limited repositioning, including Figure 7 and Tables 1-3, and the publication header changes; existing displays otherwise remain substantially unchanged.

improvement.justification: v2 adds useful FLOPs accounting, training-resource disclosure, and clearer prior-work attribution. However, Section 3.2 now calls connector validity guaranteed without additional validation, despite retaining the original limitation. Section 5.1 also asserts better downstream performance than ToME without supporting comparative results. These reporting gains and unsupported strengthenings leave the net quality direction uncertain.
